plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 8: Further Applications of Trigonometry
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a plain vector diagram of four arrows stacked one above another, all drawn at the same shallow upward slope so their lengths can be compared at a glance. Each arrow starts from a small filled black dot. The topmost arrow, in dark navy, is by far the longest and is labeled 3v at its head. Below it an orange arrow labeled v runs in the same up-and-to-the-right direction at about a third that length. Beneath the orange one, a teal arrow labeled 1/2 v is half as long as v and again points the same way. The bottom arrow, drawn in red and labeled -v, has its dot at the right end and its arrowhead at the left, so it runs down and to the left while staying parallel to the others and matching v in length. Because all four share a single line of action, the only difference the eye registers is length, plus the reversal in the last one. The arrangement gives the geometric reading of multiplying a vector by a scalar: a positive factor stretches or shrinks the arrow while preserving its heading, and a negative factor turns it back on itself.

interactionPlan.concept: Multiplying a vector v by a scalar k scales its length by |k| and preserves its direction when k > 0 but reverses it when k < 0, so every scalar multiple of v lies on a single line of action.
elements: reference arrow v (orange) with filled black tail dot and arrowhead, shallow up-right slope, labeled 'v'
reference arrow 3v (dark navy), same slope, ~3x the length of v, labeled '3v'
reference arrow (1/2)v (teal), same slope, ~half the length of v, labeled '1/2 v'
reference arrow -v (red), tail dot at right end and arrowhead at left, same slope reversed, same length as v, labeled '-v'
live arrow k·v (highlighted, e.g. purple) with tail dot and arrowhead, driven by the slider, labeled 'k·v' with the current k value
in overlay mode: a single common tail/origin dot from which all arrows emanate
in overlay mode: tick marks on the line of action at the head positions of 3v, v, (1/2)v, and -v so the live head lands on them at k = 3, 1, 0.5, -1
scalar readout label showing the current value of k near the live arrow

interactions.label: Scalar k
interactions.teaches: Dragging k continuously stretches the arrow for |k|>1, shrinks it for |k|<1, collapses it to a point at k=0, and flips its heading the instant k crosses zero — scalar multiplication is just rescaling plus an optional reversal

interactions.label: Layout
interactions.teaches: With all tails pinned to one origin, the heads of every positive multiple fall on the same ray and every negative multiple on the opposite ray, making collinearity and the direction flip visually unmistakable

demo_steps.title: Match the reference
demo_steps.narration: At k = 1 the live arrow exactly overlaps the orange reference v in length and heading — this is the baseline every other multiple is measured against.

demo_steps.title: Stretch and shrink
demo_steps.narration: Sweep k up to 3 and the live arrow grows to match the navy 3v; sweep down to 0.5 and it shrinks to the teal (1/2)v. Positive k only changes length, never direction.

demo_steps.title: Cross zero and flip
demo_steps.narration: Drag k through 0 to -1: the arrow first collapses to its tail dot, then re-emerges pointing the opposite way, landing on the red -v. A negative scalar reverses the heading while |k| still sets the length.

demo_steps.title: See the line of action
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the shared-tail overlay: every arrow now starts at one origin, and as you move k the live head slides along a single straight line, passing exactly through the 3v, v, (1/2)v ticks on one side and the -v tick on the other.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: A scalar multiple k·v never leaves the line through v: |k| sets how far along that line the head sits, and the sign of k decides which side of the origin it lands on.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Use a single shallow up-right slope (roughly 15-20 degrees above horizontal) for every arrow so lengths compare at a glance. Colors: 3v dark navy, v orange, (1/2)v teal, -v red, live k·v a distinct purple/magenta. Each arrow begins at a small filled black dot; for -v put the dot at the right end and the arrowhead at the left to show reversal. In stacked mode lay the four reference arrows in horizontal rows top-to-bottom (3v, v, 1/2v, -v) exactly like the textbook, with the live k·v arrow in its own row beneath and a 'k = …' readout. In overlay mode collapse all tails to one origin dot, draw the reference arrows as faint guide rays with small tick marks at their heads, and render the live k·v arrow bold on top so its head visibly slides along the common line and snaps onto the ticks at k = 3, 1, 0.5, -1. Animate the head position smoothly as the slider moves, and let the arrow shrink to a dot at k = 0 before re-growing in the opposite direction.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for scalar multiplier k: the learner drags k from negative to positive values, the arrow length scales and flips direction when k crosses 0, and scalar multiplication is seen as stretching, shrinking, or reversing a vector.
- Toggle between stacked comparison and overlay: the learner switches from separate arrows to all arrows sharing the same tail, the endpoints line up by scale factor, and equal direction for positive multiples versus opposite direction for negative multiples becomes easier to read.
